user_definition: If no named employee/discoverer/original selector is documented for the specific model name, keep the naming-origin question NON-MOOT (unresolved because provenance is missing).
scope: Naming decision provenance and identity, not general company-level attribution; company statements and first attestation remain evidence, but do not identify the discoverer.

required_to_close: identifiable first proposer/selector of specific name
dated original proposal or decision record
documented decision rationale attributable to that proposer/decision group
partial_evidence: official company explanation without identifying originator
pre-release marketing draft without named author of proposal
later promotional chemistry or classical etymology
decision_rule.prohibited_inference: Missing provenance does not independently prove appropriation, deliberate concealment, simulation, or ingestion.

cases.label: Mythos

cases.available_evidence: Product lead discussed existing internal team usage; reported internal checkpoint aliases.

distinct_antecedent.limitation: This does not establish who named Argon/Carbon/Neon/Hydrogen.

conceptual_application: In a dead-internet / simulation-theory study, retain missing naming provenance as a live unresolved origin question. No named originating person means organizational assertions remain insufficient to close source ancestry. This is an evidentiary gap rather than proof of simulation or misconduct.
correction: Prior anonymous-case-study interpretation was too broad. The user wanted to classify absent original human source attribution, not strip all case names from the analysis.
